requirement:
Markdown reports only `Comment` attachments. Each HTML comment block whose
trimmed text starts with `<!--` and ends with `-->` is one attachment.
An inline HTML comment within a paragraph remains paragraph text, and
comment delimiters inside fenced code remain code.
rationale:
The `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.attachments` requirement is tested by `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]`. That test carries a `{test}` reference to it. I did not read the implementation. I derived the expected behavior from the requirement text alone. For `test.md`, the test builds an `OutlineContent` snapshot. It gathers every attachment from all outline items, sorts them by span start, and asserts the exact list of `(kind, trimmed span text)` pairs. Each obligation maps to a scenario in that one source: - **Only `Comment` attachments are reported.** The expected list contains only `Comment` entries. Any `Annotation` entry, or any other attachment, would break the exact equality assertion. - **A single-line HTML comment block is one attachment.** `` must appear as `(Comment, "")`. - **A multi-line HTML comment block is one attachment.** `` must appear as a single `Comment` whose span text is the whole block. - **A non-comment HTML block is not reported.** `
html
` is in the input and absent from the expected list. - **An inline HTML comment in a paragraph stays paragraph text.** `A word.` is in the input and absent from the expected list. - **Comment delimiters inside fenced code stay code.** A ```` ```html ```` fence containing `` is in the input and absent from the expected list. - **A block that starts with `` is not a comment attachment.** The trailing ``" clause. The test also exercises the case where markdown yields several attachments, and it checks their order and exact span text. Every clause and failure case the text names has a scenario with a precise assertion, and no other marking gap applies. One untested variant is a block like ` trailing`, or several comments in one HTML block. The text does not single these out, so I do not count them as gaps.
